label: Bible Study
prompt: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot _____ thee; how much less this house that I have builded?
verse: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?
note: Solomon dedicates the temple and admits the obvious — heaven can't hold God, much less a building.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their _____.
verse: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
note: The God who counts the stars in the very next verse also bandages broken hearts.

label: Sunday School
prompt: By faith Abel offered unto God a more _____ sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
verse: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
note: Abel's offering was 'more excellent' than Cain's — and Hebrews says Abel, though dead, still speaks.

label: Deep Water
prompt: _____ yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?
verse: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?
note: Corinth had been auditing Paul's credentials; he turns the tables — check your own faith first.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many _____ proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:
verse: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:
note: Forty days of 'many infallible proofs' — Luke's case that the risen Jesus was no rumor.
